ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation 12-02; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 26 July 2019 on beneficial ownership; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2020/2840 implementing framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority or notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-Luxembourg documents; Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct (extrait de casier judiciaire) for each manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the status and identity of the incorporator(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate or private bank maintaining the initial deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if required by the Luxembourg notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and managers against PEP lists (FATF and CSSF guidance), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Luxembourg national freezing list; enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk third-country source funds; ongoing transaction monitoring and adverse media checks under CSSF Circular 19/729.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be expressed in French, German, or Luxembourgish; Latin-script transliteration is accepted; the legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' must appear; names must not be contrary to public policy and must be clearly distinguishable from existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a petition for administrative review with the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of notification, attaching additional evidence such as trademark registrations, corporate narrative, or letters of consent. If the administrative review is unsuccessful, an appeal may be brought before the Tribunal d'Arrondissement of Luxembourg under the RCS procedural rules; a final judicial remedy lies with the Cour supérieure de justice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted where provided by an approved domiciliation agent (PSF); the agent's address may serve as registered office, but the company must maintain adequate local substance (board governance, decision-making, minimal staff for licensing operations) to satisfy Luxembourg tax and ATAD substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 2–5% annual probability) for a low-risk film licensing SARL; the CSSF and tax administrations retain the right of unannounced inspections, and the probability rises to approximately 15% if the company later claims participation exemption, holding-qualifying status, or fails to file timely returns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016 on the Modernisation of Company Law; SARL governed by Articles 180 to 200; registration publicity under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies, as amended by the Law of 11 September 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, 1-7 rue du Saint-Esprit, L-1475 Luxembourg; online portal at lbr.lu / eJustice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Deed of Incorporation) executed as a notarial deed before a Luxembourg notary, filed via the Formulaire de demande d'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at formation; capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution and the blockage certificate (attestation de blocage) delivered to the notary before execution of the deed; each share must have a minimum nominal value of EUR 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers hereby incorporate a Societe a Responsabilite Limitee under Luxembourg law and irrevocably subscribe to the entirety of the issued share capital in accordance with the articles of association. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office is fixed at [Registered Office Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that the minimum statutory capital of EUR 12,000 has been deposited with a Luxembourg bank on a blocked account. RESOLVED that [Name Surname] be appointed sole gerant of the Company with full powers to represent and bind the Company, to open payment accounts, to prepare filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to appoint external auditors and counsel, and to carry out all formalities necessary to effect statutory incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked share-capital account at a Luxembourg credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), e.g. Banque Internationale a Luxembourg or Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the chosen Luxembourg bank to open an account in the name of [Company Name] SARL en formation with an express escrow blockage clause. Wire or deposit the aggregate subscription amount of at least EUR 12,000 from the shareholders' bank accounts. Request the bank to issue a capital-blockage certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary, confirming that the funds are frozen until presentation of the notarial deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Fully executed know-your-customer and beneficial-ownership declarations
Passport or national identity card copies of all subscribing shareholders
Bank reference letter or source-of-funds affidavit
Draft articles of association for bank due diligence review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial ownership or source of funds, submit a notarised explanation, audited financial statements of corporate shareholders, and documentary evidence tracing the funds; escalate any unresolved query to the bank's legal and compliance department and, if necessary, select an alternative CSSF-licensed credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the deed of incorporation before a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg - individual notary empowered to authenticate Luxembourg company deeds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary with the requested corporate name, registered office address, share distribution, and the identity of the first gerant. The notary will verify name availability via the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Central Valuation Office databases, draft the articles of association under Articles 180 to 200 of the Law of 10 August 1915, and collect the capital-blockage certificate. Subscribers must appear before the notary or be represented by a notarised and apostilled power of attorney. Upon signature of the deed, the company is validly constituted with legal personality, subject to the subsequent RCS registration and publication formalities.
required_dossiers: Capital-blockage attestation issued by the Luxembourg bank
Valid passports or identity cards of founders and of the appointed gerant
Apostilled powers of attorney for any remotely represented shareholder
Board extract and constitutional documents of any corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused or the notary identifies a formal defect in the powers of attorney, promptly execute an amending power of attorney or select an alternative corporate name; any post-execution correction is made by a supplementary notarial deed (acte rectificatif).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, electronic filing via the lbr.lu / eJustice portal or in person at the RCS desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic or paper registration application together with the notarial deed of incorporation, the completed RCS registration form signed by the gerant, the bank blockage certificate if not already annexed to the deed, and the specimen signature of the gerant. Pay the statutory registration fee of EUR 19 for electronic filing or EUR 26 for paper filing, plus the RESA publication charge. The RCS registrar verifies compliance with the mandatory legal content and issues the official registration extract (extrait du registre).
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed of incorporation
Completed RCS registration form (formulaire de demande d'inscription)
Specimen signature card of the gerant
Copy of identity documents of the gerant and shareholders
Proof of payment of the registration and publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing annexes or inconsistent information, counsel or the notary must respond within the statutory delay of 15 days; if the refusal persists, the matter can be referred to the supervisory jurisdiction of the district court (tribunal d'arrondissement) in Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation in the Recueil Electronique des Societes et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - official electronic compendium of companies and associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the RCS registration, the registrar automatically transmits the deed of incorporation to RESA for legal publication. Verify that the publication appears within the statutory period of 10 business days and contains the required particulars. The RESA publication makes the deed opposable to third parties and perfects the statutory publicity required by the Law of 19 December 2002; third parties may rely on the published information from the registration date.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract confirming the registration number
Notarial deed of incorporation transmitted automatically by the RCS
Registered-address and purpose particulars as published in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or erroneous, request a corrective notice from LBR and obtain a confirmation certificate of publication; notify key counterparties and, if any third party suffers prejudice, instruct counsel to seek a judicial correction order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation fiscal, social security and business license formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Securite Sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Ministry of the Economy - Direction de l'autorisation d'etablissement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of RCS registration, file the VAT registration form with the AEDT business tax office and obtain a Luxembourg VAT number. Register the SARL and any employees with the CCSS for social security coverage. File the prior written declaration of office opening with the ITM at least 8 days before the commencement of operations. Assess whether the film-copyright distribution and licensing activity constitutes a commercial profession under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions; where the company acts solely as an intellectual-property holding and licensing vehicle, no autorisation d'etablissement is required, but an application must be filed if physical media distribution or active trading is undertaken.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
VAT declaration form 601 for securing a Luxembourg TVA number
CCSS registration form and payroll information
ITM office-opening declaration
Business license application and professional integrity certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT challenges the economic reality of the licensing activity, provide the RCS business-purpose extract together with specimen copyright distribution agreements; an adverse decision on the autorisation d'etablissement can be administratively appealed to the Ministry of the Economy and subsequently to the administrative tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction de l'autorisation d'etablissement, Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial establishment permit mandated for pure motion-picture international copyright distribution and licensing; if physical media master storage is introduced, a classified-establishment notification under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement - Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category II negative screening; the activity is an office-based intellectual-property licensing operation with no industrial installation, no combustion plant, and no polluting production process, hence no full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial wastewater or VOCs; the office premises must comply with municipal wastewater connection rules under the law of 19 December 2008 on water management, and any electronic-waste or film-archive waste must be handled in accordance with the WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and national waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGIDS) and the competent municipal authority is required for office premises with a surface exceeding 500 m2 or an occupant load of over 100 persons, including evacuation plans, fire-extinguishing equipment, and electrical installation verification; the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) must receive the prior written opening declaration and the workplace must satisfy the health, lighting, ventilation, ergonomic, and first-aid requirements of the Luxembourg Labor Code; structural load clearance applies where open-shelf storage of physical film prints is maintained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (corporate income tax, net wealth tax, withholding tax) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) / Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Administration (VAT and registration duties). The unified electronic portal is MyGuichet.lu (www.guichet.lu); company registration is managed by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: [1] Incorporate the SARL before a Luxembourg notary with a minimum share capital of EUR 12,000; register within one month in the RCS via the e-Registration platform 'LBR.lu'. The RCS issues the company's 13-digit national identification number ('matricule'), which serves as the corporate tax identification number for all direct tax purposes; no separate ACD registration is required. [2] For VAT, file the official application Form 640 electronically via MyGuichet.lu, or for non-established foreign entities Form 644 (simplified registration of non-established taxable persons), attaching the amended articles of association, RCS extract, proof of the manager's identity and power of attorney if a VAT representative is appointed. The AEDT issues the VAT identification number in the format 'LU' + 8 digits, normally within 2-4 weeks. [3] Non-resident companies not incorporated in Luxembourg that perform taxable supplies in the country (e.g., active film licensing distributed to Luxembourg-based licensees outside a reverse-charge scenario) must obtain a Luxembourg VAT number before commencing operations; a fiscal representative may be required if the third-country company has no permanent establishment in the EU. [4] If hiring staff, register as an employer with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) and with the ACD for payroll withholding; since the SARL produces no requirement for an activity licence in the video/film distribution sector, no additional regulatory tax clearing is needed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (opaque taxpayer). The SARL is a Luxembourg tax-resident company taxed on worldwide income: corporate income tax (IRC) at a flat 17% headline rate, an unemployment/solidarity surcharge of 7% on IRC, and the municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) at a communal rate of 6.75% in Luxembourg City, leading to an aggregate corporate tax burden of approximately 24.94% for the 2024/2025 fiscal year. Net wealth tax of 0.5% applies (0.05% on the portion of taxable net wealth exceeding EUR 500 million). The participation exemption regime (Art. 166 LIR) exempts qualifying dividends and capital gains from IRC and net wealth tax. The tax scope is worldwide but a territorial approach applies only to non-resident taxpayers taxed on Luxembourg-source income; there is no tax-exempt zone regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; the SARL is irrebuttably opaque under the Luxembourg corporate income tax code. Available elections and statutory regimes of relevance: (i) VAT group election ('assujetti unique', Art. 60 Luxembourg VAT law) allowing the SARL and its close economic, financial, and organisational links to file as a single taxable person; (ii) corporate fiscal unity election (Art. 164bis LIR) for a resident parent holding at least 95% of a resident subsidiary, enabling profit/loss offset; (iii) notional interest deduction (NID) election on increases in qualifying equity; (iv) IP box election granting an 80% exemption of qualifying intellectual property income (must be declared with the annual tax return and substantiated with qualifying IP assets and development evidence); (v) participation exemption is mandatory once the 10% or EUR 1.2 million holding threshold and substance conditions are met, with no separate election; (vi) hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD II apply automatically and cannot be elected out; (vii) SCSp-type fiscally transparent vehicles are available at constitution but are not relevant to a classic SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (VAT) / 'Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée' (TVA), governed by the amended law of 12 February 1979 transposing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the domestic micro-business exemption under Art. 57a VAT law; revenue above EUR 35,000 triggers mandatory VAT registration in Luxembourg. For non-established foreign suppliers there is no turnover threshold - registration is mandatory before carrying out any taxable transaction in Luxembourg, subject to the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) simplification for distance sales of goods up to EUR 10,000 and for electronically supplied services to non-taxable persons, in which case the supplier can declare VAT in its home Member State instead of registering in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time tax clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), API-based revenue stamping, or fiscal digital stamping regime is in force in Luxembourg as of 2025. E-invoices are accepted only with the recipient's consent; paper and PDF invoices are still valid. In line with the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' directive adopted on 11 March 2025, Luxembourg is required to transpose mandatory structured e-invoicing obligations for intra-EU B2B transactions by 30 June 2028, with the actual mandatory issuance of e-invoices from 1 July 2030; until then, invoice storage must guarantee authenticity, integrity, and legibility for the statutory 10-year retention period, and there is no requirement to pre-clear invoices electronically with the AEDT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical exports of goods (e.g., film masters, hard drives, marketing materials) dispatched to a destination outside the EU, a 0% VAT rate applies provided the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days and are evidenced by a customs export declaration. For the independent film licensing business model of the LU_SARL, the predominant cross-border supplies are licensing services / royalties: intra-EU B2B licensing of copyrights and film rights is outside Luxembourg VAT, with the customer self-assessing VAT under reverse charge; B2B licensing to third-country licensees is outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (place of supply is the customer's jurisdiction); B2C electronically supplied content to foreign consumers is taxable where the consumer is established (OSS may be used for EU consumers). Thus, classic 'export zero-rating' on goods is the exception, while the zero/no-VAT outcome on licensing services is achieved through place-of-supply and reverse-charge mechanisms, requiring commercial and payment documentation rather than a customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Déclaration d'exportation, lodged electronically in the EU ICS/ECAX customs system) for physical goods; not applicable to pure intellectual property licensing flows in the absence of tangible goods.
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, air waybill, or certified postal receipt evidencing physical dispatch of film materials outside the EU, where applicable.
Executed licence agreement containing the IP description, territory, duration, royalty formula, and clear identification of the foreign licensee (relevant in all licensing scenarios).

Commercial tax invoice issued by the LU_SARL referencing the place-of-supply rule, the customer's VAT registration number validated through VIES, and the reverse-charge mention for intra-EU B2B services.
Bank credit evidence (SWIFT / MT103, bank statement, or letter of credit settlement) showing the inward remittance of the royalty consideration to the SARL's Luxembourg bank account.
Proof of the licensee's establishment: foreign trade register extract, OECD/EU VAT certificate, or a certificate of tax residence when the licensor claims no-Luxembourg-VAT treatment.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg imposes no statutory foreign-currency repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure serves as the practical documentation benchmark used by the AEDT and ACD for verifying that the underlying export/licensing transaction is genuine and economically performed. Under the VAT law (Art. 82-89), failure to produce the required export or place-of-supply evidence results in: (i) reassessment of VAT at the full 17% standard rate on the gross royalty amount, with no deduction for foreign input VAT; (ii) late-payment interest of 0.8% per month (9.6% p.a.); (iii) administrative fines from EUR 250 to EUR 6,000 per infraction, and up to EUR 12,500 for fraudulent concealment; (iv) a standard limitation period of 5 years for reassessment, extended to 10 years in the case of fraud, simulated operation, or abuse of law (abus fiscal under Art. 6 AStG / Art. 89 LDIR). Criminal prosecution may be initiated under the general criminal law and the Luxembourg tax fraud statute with imprisonment up to 5 years where the licensing documentation is fabricated or where the structure lacks genuine economic substance; the AEDT's audit division specifically examines cross-border royalty chains for artificial conduit arrangements, mandatory substance requirements, and the economic reality of the film licensing rights.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as national central bank within the Eurosystem, jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and AML supervision, and the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro monetary policy and payments oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible across both current and capital account transactions in Luxembourg. EU Treaty Articles 63-66 TFEU and the EMU legal framework guarantee complete freedom of capital movements, with no residual exchange-control restrictions. Profit remittance is unrestricted; dividend distributions attract a 15% domestic withholding tax unless reduced under the Luxembourg participation exemption, a bilateral tax treaty, or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. Cross-border royalty payments are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, which materially facilitates treasury flows for an independent film licensing SARL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Luxembourg. Export and royalty receipts may be retained indefinitely in EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency in resident or non-resident accounts without BCL licensing. The only macro-relevant obligation is statistical reporting to the BCL under the balance-of-payments framework, requiring the settlement data and classification codes for transactions above specified de minimis thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account and dedicated Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with SWIFT/MT103 rail and subsidiary Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and segregated Escrow for royalty holdbacks
Operational Account and wealth-linked treasury sweep structure
Operational Account for euro-area SEPA clearing and trade finance lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. EU-passported EMI and fintech platforms such as Wise Business, Revolut Business, and Payoneer provide rapid low-cost collection of global streaming and theatrical royalties, but they should be treated strictly as secondary operational rails. They are not viable for capital escrow, standby letters of credit, documentary collections, or BCL statistical reporting and cannot replace a Luxembourg-authorised credit institution for high-value IP transactions. Any EMI must be restricted to sub-posting accounts with a twice-monthly sweep to the tier-1 bank to maintain audit integrity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid with strong physical presumption. Leading Luxembourg banks generally require a physical onboarding interview with at least one director or a Luxembourg domiciliation agent holding a notarised power of attorney. Remote video KYC is tolerated only for low-risk non-resident directors if the SARL maintains a Luxembourg registered office, a Luxembourg corporate secretary under CSSF supervision, and acceptable certified documentation. Given CSSF circular 2019/01 diligence expectations, a notarised proxy interview is the fastest compliant route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-only revenue model with royalty counterparties headquartered in high-risk or preferential-regime territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chain-of-title legal opinion from a Luxembourg notary; executed movie distribution and sub-licensing agreements with territorial schedules; ISAN registry specimen; sound recording and audiovisual rights assignment deeds; sworn source-of-funds declarations from all UBOs; audited P&L of the SARL evidencing real licensing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared corporate purpose and inbound wire volumes lacking underlying commercial documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved Treasury and Substance Policy letter; invoice and credit-note register referenced to each license; per-title distribution statements from the sales agent; a digital dossier linking each SWIFT MT103 to a specific licensing invoice; signed bank mandate granting periodic compliance-audit access to the external AML officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funds velocity through thinly-documented payment processors or nominee collection accounts in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approved list of collection agents and payment rails; anti-money-laundering due-diligence file for each agent including FATF country risk rating and corporate registry abstracts; automated reconciliation report of end-customer receipts versus distributor statements; Luxembourg substance folder with lease, payroll, and board meeting minutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO structure with high-value single-transaction IP transfers that may hint at IP migration and profit stripping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO Register filing in Luxembourg (RBE); enhanced due-diligence pack including PEP screening and media background verification; full holding structure diagram with economic owner rationale; independent IP valuation certificate from an international audit firm; evidence of compliance with Luxembourg substance rules including local staff costs and administrative premises.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity injection must be executed via SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pain.001 messages using the external purpose code 'EQUI' (equity) or the BCL balance-of-payments category for direct investment equity, with the beneficiary account expressly designated as the Capital Escrow Account. The injection must be supported by a notarised capital increase deed of the Luxembourg SARL, meeting the minimum EUR 12,000 share capital requirement with full payment in cash through the bank. Transactions equal to or above EUR 1,000,000 trigger BCL statistical declaration duties; remitters must provide a source-of-wealth statement and an executed board resolution authorising the capital call.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Euro-area operating payments clear via SEPA Credit Transfer using pain.001.001.03 XML files. Non-EEA settlements must route through SWIFT MT103 cover payments for distributor commission, DCP mastering, subtitle and technical services, and inter-company fees. Trade settlements are additionally supported by documentary collections (DP/DA) for against-documents release of licensed film materials and by Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 by a Luxembourg confirming bank when licensees demand delivery guarantees. All outbound disbursements are matched against the licensed territory schedules and marketing budget approvals, and foreign-currency disbursements above treasury thresholds require two-signature dual control on the tier-1 platform.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Plain Vanilla FX Forward with tenors up to 24 months for streaming and North American licensing receipts
EUR/GBP FX Forward for United Kingdom theatrical and broadcasting royalty flows
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) referencing restricted-convertibility currencies where the film licensing contract is settled via a distributor netting arrangement
FX Swap for tom-next rollover of accrued foreign-currency royalty balances into EUR liquidity
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) to hedge currency risk on any treasury-backed financing line secured against the copyright catalogue
European-Style FX Option Collar on USD/EUR to protect a minimum guaranteed royalty stream while preserving upside participation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year end, but no later than 7 months for the general meeting approval; filing within 1 month of approval and always by 31 December of the following year for standard calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 5,000 per director (Law of 19 December 2002, Art. 1); administrative strike-off after repeated non-filing and formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune, IFT) and annual subscription tax (taxe d'abonnement) declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Registration Duties and Estates Agency (AEDT) for subscription tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Net wealth tax return due 31 December of the tax year (or 28 February following year for e-filing); subscription tax due annually by 31 March for the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late payment penalty, 0.6% monthly interest on arrears; additional penalties for false declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 31 December of the following tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; extension available on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty 10% of tax due (min EUR 100); 0.6% monthly interest; criminal fines for imminent fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of any change; if no change, annual confirmation filed within 31 December of each year referencing prior declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 per violation; directors personally liable for false filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual meeting minutes and agenda (approval of annual accounts, discharge of managers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with authorities; retained in corporate minute book; submitted upon request to RCS or tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held within 6 months of financial year end; minutes executed within one month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Invalidity of decisions if formal requirements not met; liability of managers for failure to call meeting

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (réviseur d'entreprises) if any two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total balance sheet EUR 6,000,000, net turnover EUR 12,200,000, average employees 50; public-interest entities and certain financial/credit institutions always audited
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg legal chart of accounts) per Law of 19 December 2002; IFRS (as adopted by EU) permitted for consolidated financial statements and optional for individual accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must maintain an RBE register and annually confirm the beneficial ownership details. A confirmation filing is required each calendar year even if no ownership change occurs; any transfer of shares triggering indirect ownership change must be declared within 30 days of the event. Full chain-of-title evidence for share transfers retained 5 years after cessation of status.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,500 - 4,500 USD (typical Luxembourg registered agent & domiciliation service annual fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 12,000 USD (for small to mid-size SARL with compulsory audit, subject to scope)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% national corporate income tax (IRC) on taxable income above EUR 175,000, plus a 7% employment-fund surcharge, giving a headline national rate of 18.19%; municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) adds approximately 6.75% in Luxembourg City, producing a blended statutory burden of about 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays; preferential 80% exemption for qualifying intellectual property income under the Luxembourg IP box (Article 50ter LIR), yielding an effective rate near 3.4%–5.0% on eligible IP net income; certain R&D tax credits and an innovation box are available; film copyrights may qualify only if the asset meets the modified nexus requirements and is actively managed.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (unlimited carryforward), but for losses incurred after 1 January 2017 offset in any tax year is capped at 90% of the taxable income, preserving a 10% minimum taxation base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 3 – Déclaration d’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités (annual corporate income tax return); filed electronically through the ACD portal on MyGuichet.lu with a LuxTrust authentication certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one return per fiscal year for each Luxembourg-resident SARL, even in the absence of taxable profit.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due by 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end; a three-month automatic extension is available to 30 September, and further administrative extensions are granted when the return is prepared by a licensed tax adviser (commonly to 31 December).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg RCS registration number, legal form (SARL), registered office, tax identification number, fiscal-year dates, and parent/shareholder details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate taxpayer with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must identify the PE branch code and local agent; for a resident SARL wholly held by non-residents, the ultimate shareholding group and DTA eligibility must be clearly disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income for the accounting period according to Luxembourg GAAP financial statements, before tax charges and after depreciation, provisions, and exceptional items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must reconcile the Luxembourg PE net profit to the taxable base; attach the local statutory accounts and a reconciliation schedule showing adjustments for foreign-source exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses absorbed against current-year taxable income, including the required statutory cap calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For losses generated after 1 January 2017, do not offset more than 90% of the current-year taxable base; a separate schedule of carried-forward losses and loss year must accompany the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net qualifying IP income, including film copyright royalties where the asset is a qualifying IP right under Article 50ter LIR, after the 80% exemption is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident applicants must ensure the qualifying IP asset is owned and economically developed through the Luxembourg entity; attach nexus calculations, IP asset inventory, and substance evidence such as local board minutes, personnel records, and license contracts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty up to EUR 3,000 per return; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum) from the statutory due date; where fraud or gross negligence is established, an additional penalty of 10%–50% of the understated tax may be imposed, and criminal fines of up to EUR 250,000 for wilful evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax is 15% on gross distributions to shareholders, including de facto profit-sharing payments and similar income; the rate is reduced to 0% for qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive shareholders holding at least 10% of the SARL share capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period; under applicable double tax treaties, rates may further be reduced to 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on the shareholding and LOB provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a tax-residency certificate (TRC) from its competent tax authority, complete the Luxembourg withholding-tax relief form or reclaim form, and submit it to the tax administration through the withholding agent; a prior treaty-exemption certificate may be obtained from ACD before distribution, otherwise a reclaim must be filed within the applicable limitation period (generally five years) with a detailed beneficial ownership declaration; EU parent companies claim the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption by providing a P1 form / certificate of residence and substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law generally does not impose withholding tax on arm's-length royalties or ordinary debt interest paid to non-residents; interest on profit-sharing bonds and certain equity-like instruments is treated as a dividend and taxed at 15%; royalty payments sourced from Luxembourg to non-resident licensors are not subject to domestic WHT, although treaty source taxation may be retained at 0%–5% when the income is derived through a Luxembourg PE; all such payments remain subject to transfer pricing and ATAD anti-abuse review.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Luxembourg Local File is mandatory when the resident entity's cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 500,000 for goods or tangible assets, or EUR 150,000 for services, financing, royalties, and intangibles; a Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated turnover reaches EUR 750 million; the documentation must be contemporaneous and filed within 30 days of the tax authority's request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations statute like UAE/offshore regimes, but the ATAD General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 6 LIR), BEPS treaty substance requirements, and the IP box's 'business activity' condition all require a real economic presence; a film-licensing SARL must demonstrate local staff with decision-making authority, an own office, board minutes approving licensing terms, active monitoring of licensees, and a substantive royalty account; otherwise the IP box, treaty benefits, and deduction for intercompany royalties will be denied under the principle that the conduit entity lacks economic reality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or misstatement of taxable royalty income, concealment of bank accounts, creation of false license agreements to shift profits, or false declaration of deductible expenses in the film-licensing SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment of the hidden profit, late-interest charge of 7.2% per annum, administrative penalties of 10% to 50% of the evaded tax, and criminal conviction punishable by fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; the court may also order restitution of fiscal losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors that participate in or knowingly approve evasion are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, subject to civil restitution, personal asset seizure, travel bans restricting movement from EU territory, and imprisonment where criminal fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Luxembourg SARL as a bare mailbox vehicle with no own premises, employees, or independent commercial activity, used merely as a channeling intermediary to route film royalties from end-users into tax-haven affiliates while retaining no genuine licensing management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits, withdrawal of the IP box exemption, recharacterization of accumulated royalties as constructive dividends subject to 15% withholding tax, penal reassessment, and possible fine under the General Tax Law; under ATAD, the arrangement may be disregarded and taxed as in the substantive owner's hands.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the SARL is used as a pure sham; directors become jointly and severally liable for the full tax deficiency, repatriation of illicitly shifted profits, personal travel restrictions pending criminal investigation, and imprisonment for complicity in tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or produce the Luxembourg Local File and Master File, absence of a written contract for film-licensing intercompany transactions, or setting royalty rates with no comparable benchmark and no active substance, resulting in an arbitrary non-arm's-length remuneration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities may upwardly adjust the Luxembourg taxable profit to an arm's-length margin, deny the deduction of excess royalty payments, and impose late-payment interest; administrative penalties for non-production of documentation can reach up to 10% of the resulting adjustment, and if negligence is evidenced, an additional fine of up to EUR 100,000 may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Chief officers who signed or caused the flawed transfer-pricing policy to be adopted are jointly liable for the resulting recovery, may face administrative fines, be disqualified as directors for up to 5 years, and in cases of deliberate mispricing be subject to criminal sanctions including travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the film-licensing SARL's Swift wire and letter-of-credit payment rails to receive or disburse royalties from undisclosed beneficial owners, sanctioned jurisdictions, or in cash-like structures without executing customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification, or filing suspicious activity reports with the Luxembourg FIU (Cellule Renseignement Financier).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Luxembourg AML Law (Law of 12 November 2004) of up to EUR 5 million; the SARL's corporate registration may be struck from the RCS, its bank accounts frozen, and the tax administration may impose an additional 15% gross-up on non-compliant payments; asset freezes apply in economic-sanctions cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal criminal liability for money-laundering and sanctions breaches, including criminal fines, seizure of personal assets, travel bans (EDTFA measures), and imprisonment up to 5 years; the corporate veil may be pierced under the AML law to reach the controlling persons, and professional sector bans are commonly imposed.
